highlights.title: The Bentley Supersports: A stripped-out engineer's indulgence
highlights.summary: Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Supersports, as well as ride in a preproduction Torcal EV, which we wrote about last week. Ars does not accept paid editorial content.
body: MONTEREY, Calif.—Last week, we brought news of the Bentley Torcal, a new electric vehicle that the luxury automaker has been cooking up at its HQ in Crewe, England. The company wants to attract new customers with its first battery EV, part of a plan to make sustainability as much a part of the brand's character as its high-end fit and finish. W12 engines have given way to V8 plug-in hybrid power, and the new Continental GT is all the better for it.

But around the same time as Ars got its first experience of that new PHEV two-door on a rather wet Spanish racetrack, some of Bentley's boffins were wondering what might happen if you also built one without the hybrid stuff.

Or all-wheel drive—something that has been a characteristic of every new road-going Bentley since the turn of the century. That would certainly cut the curb weight. So, too, would leaving out the rear seats. That sort of idea leads down a well-trodden path for some OEMs, and Porsche in particular is famous for making stripped-out road cars inspired by its race cars and making money from them, too.

highlights.title: MIT Quantum Initiative launches postdoctoral fellowship program
highlights.summary: The Institute welcomes its first cohort of QMIT Fellows this fall to advance interdisciplinary quantum research.
body: The MIT Quantum Initiative (QMIT) has launched a new postdoctoral fellowship program to accelerate interdisciplinary quantum research and develop the next generation of scientific leaders working at the frontiers of quantum science and technology.

Supported by a grant from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation, the program reflects QMIT’s vision of expanding the boundaries of quantum science by encouraging researchers to connect quantum approaches with other disciplines and emerging applications.

As opportunities in quantum research expand, investing in outstanding early-career researchers has never been more important. These fellowships are designed to help cultivate the next generation of quantum leaders, providing the resources and collaborative environment needed to advance transformative research at MIT.

highlights.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
highlights.summary: Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.
body: This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

highlights.title: Gal Gadot Says James Gunn and Peter Safran Told Her Wonder Woman 3 Was Happening Before Its Messy Cancellation
highlights.summary: Former DC movie star Gal Gadot has opened up about the confusion surrounding Wonder Woman 3, saying that, even though it "wasn't handled elegantly," it's "all good" between her, James Gunn, and Peter Safran. The story of Wonder Woman 3 is a bit of a mess.
body: One of the stranger updates during the kerfuffle saw the actress confirm the two superhero film execs had told her she would come back as Diana Prince for Wonder Woman 3 before it was reported that Gunn and Safran didn't have any plans for a third movie from director Patty Jenkins after all. It was a back-and-forth painful enough to watch from the outside, but it was probably even more grueling on the inside.

Gadot recalled the confusion during an interview with Happy, Sad, Confused. She again confirmed that Gunn and Safran assured her Wonder Woman 3 was happening, going as far as to say that there was never a clear moment when the project was formally canned.

"No, they told me the opposite," she answered when asked about the circumstances surrounding the cancellation. "They were like, 'We're going to develop it with you, [Wonder Woman 3], but I saw the way everybody else was handled, right?"

highlights.title: The Hugging Face hack could indicate cultural issues at OpenAI
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. By now you’ve probably heard about last month’s major AI security incident, in which OpenAI agents escaped their sandbox and hacked into the AI platform Hugging…
body: The day before OpenAI released that report, I spoke with David Krueger, a computer science professor and prominent alignment expert who took leave from the University of Montreal to found and lead an AI safety nonprofit called Evitable. He said what he had really hoped to see in the report was an analysis of the human factors behind the incident.

“When you look at accidents and incidents, oftentimes people try to find the technical source of failure, but that can give a very inaccurate and misleading sense of why the failure occurred,” he said. “If people are just cutting corners all the time, if people are not in a culture that prioritizes safety and has appropriate incentives and structures, [accidents] are kind of bound to happen.”

The report did not meet Krueger’s hopes. Its 38 pages detail a multi-month progression of agent misbehavior that culminated in the Hugging Face hack, explore the technical reasons why that misbehavior occurred, and enumerate the steps being taken to prevent similar events in the future. But there’s no consideration of the role that company culture may have played in the incident, and the report includes few references to specific human errors.

highlights.title: 33 years later, Tombstone's final line is still the greatest quote in Western movie history
highlights.summary: Tombstone is often considered one of the greatest Westerns ever made, and for good reason. This is a movie that features a star-studded cast, including Kurt Russell and Val Kilmer, plenty of intense fights, and some surprisingly emotional scenes between its hardened gunslingers.
body: The closing moments of Tombstone are bittersweet, as Wyatt Earp (Russell) and his posse take down the notorious Cowboys. Earp then decides to pursue a quiet life with his lover, Josephine Marcus (Dana Delany). As Earp and Josephine start dancing in freshly fallen snow, Mitchum's voice cuts in to reveal the legendary gunslinger's fate. "Wyatt Earp died in Los Angeles in 1929. Among the pallbearers at his funeral were early Western stars William S. Hart and Tom Mix. Tom Mix wept," the narration gravely intones. It's those three words that hit hardest, especially if you know who Tom Mix is.

Tom Mix is one of the first actors to truly define the Western, thanks to his appearances in over 100 movies. Most portray Mix in a way that helped shape the Western protagonist — a white hat, carrying twin six-shooters, and driven by a desire for justice. Mix's on-screen persona was modeled on Wyatt Earp, and the two even became friends later in life. Earp would often visit Mix on the set of his movies, and even gifted Mix one of his pocket watches. Not many people can say they became friends with an actual living legend, so it's no surprise that Mix cried at Earp's funeral.

highlights.title: Amazon rigged billions in ad pricing, lawsuit from states and US watchdog alleges
highlights.summary: Amazon responded to the lawsuit, arguing the US Federal Trade Commission "misunderstands" their ad market.
body: The US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and a bipartisan group of 22 states has filed a lawsuit alleging Amazon secretly overcharged more than a million advertising customers by manipulating online auctions it uses to set ad prices.
The FTC and states say in their lawsuit filed Monday that the alleged scheme has likely netted the company $20bn from advertising customers since 2019.
"Amazon overrides and replaces the actual auction results with higher prices set by Amazon to increase its profits," says a complaint filed in the company's home state of Washington.
In a statement to the BBC, Amazon "strongly disagrees" with the premise that it misled advertisers and called the suit "misguided."

highlights.title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
highlights.summary: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.
body: The Pentagon has launched versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok, giving 3 million civilian and military personnel access to generative AI tools that have been tailored to “warfighter needs.”
ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government — custom versions of the popular consumer generative AI tools — are now part of GenAI.mil, a centralized, secure portal launched last year.

GenAI.mil, which offered Google Gemini when it first launched, is designed to give Department of Defense employees access to commercial frontier AI models without sending sensitive government data through ordinary consumer channels. In particular, the official military version is exempt from the data collection that is difficult to avoid in consumer tech products.

And according to the Department of Defense, the generative AI portal has proven popular. GenAI.mil has already onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users out of the department’s 3 million personnel, according to the department.
points: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.

highlights.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker PC Settings Guide: Maximize Your PC Performance By Tweaking These Options
highlights.summary: While 2026 has so far been packed with incredible PC games, The Blood of Dawnwalker was the one that I was looking forward to the most. Not only does it come from a game director with an incredible pedigree, but ever since system requirements were first revealed in February, I knew that this game…
body: Luckily, Rebel Wolves has since lightened the system requirements a bit, now only recommending an RTX 4070 Ti for 4K 60 fps gameplay, rather than the RTX 5090 I thought it was going to require at the beginning of the year. And now that I’ve had a chance to play it, I’m pleasantly surprised at its performance, even if the visuals are a little mixed.

Just like a lot of RPGs of this scope, much of what makes The Blood of Dawnwalker so beautiful is its environments. Just walking through the town and the forest in the opening chapter is jaw-dropping, with realistic foliage and water. The character models don’t quite reach the same fidelity, but I’m ok with that when just walking through the world looks as good as it does.

While The Blood of Dawnwalker is available on Xbox Series X and PlayStation 5, PC is where it truly shines. This game has pretty much every graphics option I’d like in a modern game, and avoids clumping a bunch of graphics techniques into one banner. The game is quite heavy to run maxed out, but there is genuinely enough room to dial it in for better performance, pretty much whichever hardware you’re playing it on.

highlights.title: Trump Calls for Passage of Federal Film and TV Tax Incentive: “Let’s Get This Done!”
highlights.summary: The bill already had bipartisan support, but Republican lawmakers especially seemed to be waiting to see if the President would support the idea.
body: For some time now, the idea of a federal film and television tax incentive has had bipartisan support, but Republican lawmakers have seemingly been waiting on word from the White House.

Now, it appears, that word has come. On Monday, President Donald Trump posted that he wants to “get this done“ in a lengthy Truth Social message expressing support for the idea of a federal tax credit.

The president added, “Meetings are being set up with the Leaders of both Parties in order to get this done. It should be Bipartisan, especially since so much money is being lost in California, and other largely Blue States. I am going to suggest that Republicans and Democrats get together, and immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America.”

The president then exhorted Congress to approve such legislation, which would provide films and TV shows that shoot in the U.S. with incentives that they could stack on top of individual states’ tax credits. “What we watch on the Silver Screen should be made in what was once the Movie and Motion Picture Capital of the World. Let’s get this done!” Trump concluded.
points: The bill already had bipartisan support, but Republican lawmakers especially seemed to be waiting to see if the President would support the idea.

highlights.title: Trump admin shelves Cyclospora research despite record-breaking outbreak
highlights.summary: The Trump administration is halting vital federal research on the foodborne parasite Cyclospora, despite the record-breaking, nationwide outbreak of the diarrheal pathogen, according to Politico.
body: Of the three research programs that represent nearly all of the Cyclospora work at the US Department of Agriculture, two have been defunded, and the third is about to lose every scientist working on it. The Trump administration is shuttering the USDA’s Beltsville Agricultural Research Center near Washington, DC, and moving its work to a location in Iowa. That includes relocating the remaining Cyclospora research.

Although the research is still funded, insiders told Politico that not one of the scientists working on the project plans to relocate from Maryland to Iowa. Instead, they are either retiring, being reassigned to a different project, or leaving the USDA’s research services.
“They will have no parasitologists,” one USDA employee told Politico. “There will be a big knowledge gap.”

The US is experiencing the largest Cyclospora outbreak ever recorded. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has tallied nearly 30,000 confirmed and probable cases this summer. At least 922 people have been hospitalized with cyclosporiasis, and two have died. Since 2018, the US has generally reported between 2,000 and 5,000 cases, though the US reported 1,180 cases in 2025.

highlights.title: New York Governor Kathy Hochul thinks AI should be ‘less evil’
highlights.summary: Today, I’m talking with New York Governor Kathy Hochul, and I’ll just warn you — this episode moves really fast. It’s an election year, after all, with a shocking amount of tech policy at stake, and Governor Hochul has taken strong positions on almost every major tech issue there is.
body: For example, Meta just reached a settlement with dozens of states, including New York, which will restrict how teens use platforms like Instagram in very specific ways. Governor Hochul is a strong supporter of those restrictions and more, as you’ll hear. But those come with a cost — widespread age verification means adults will also have to show ID to use the internet, which will essentially make it impossible to be anonymous online.

So I asked about that, and if these new restrictions amount to Meta conceding in a lawsuit that these kinds of regulations on speech might not pass First Amendment scrutiny if the governor were to try and impose them in a law.

I had similar questions about New York’s restrictions on ghost guns, which prevent 3D printers from printing gun parts. That law is already being challenged — not in courts, but by activists like Cody Wilson, who runs the largest database of 3D-printable gun files and who has started altering those files in a process he calls “Hochulization” in order to show the ban is technically toothless. I asked the governor about this, and, well, you’ll hear her challenge Cody right back.

highlights.title: Harry Edward, Britain’s first black Olympic medallist, inducted into England Athletics hall of fame
highlights.summary: Edward and Mo Farah among those to be inducted. Sonia Lannaman and Shirley Strong also honoured. Britain’s first black Olympic medal winner Harry Edward is to be inducted into the England Athletics Hall of Fame.
body: Edward was until recent years a forgotten hero of the 1920s, a decade that saw him win two bronze edals, in the 100m and 200m, at the 1920 Antwerp Olympics. He was also three times the AAA 100yd and 220yd champion and won the 100, 220 and 440-yard AAA championships in 1922, inside a single hour. King George V came down from the stands to personally congratulate him.
Soon afterwards he emigrated to the US and disappeared from view. When he died in 1973 not a single British newspaper published a line to mark his passing.

Born and raised in Berlin, he was forging a promising career as a teenage sprinter when the first world war began. His father came from the British colony of Dominica, so Edward was arrested and interned. After the war he went to London, joined the Polytechnic Harriers and ran for Britain in the Olympics. Harold Abrahams, the British sprinter immortalised in Chariots of Fire, regarded him as one of the greatest sprinters he ever saw. He never beat him.

highlights.title: Trump Endorses U.S. Tax Incentive to Keep Hollywood Production: ‘Let’s Get This Done!’
highlights.summary: President Trump on Monday endorsed a federal tax incentive for film and TV production, a move long sought by Hollywood studios and unions. In a statement posted to Truth Social, Trump said he will push for a bipartisan bill to save the industry.
body: Several Democratic lawmakers have gotten behind the idea, notably including Sen. Adam Schiff, who held a hearing on the topic in March. But Schiff and others have said that Republican lawmakers were waiting on a positive signal from the White House getting on board.
Charles Rivkin, the CEO of the Motion Picture Association, applauded Trump’s move in a statement.

“For over a century, American studios, casts, and crews have produced the films and series that the world wants to see,” Rivkin said. “A federal incentive would be a landmark step toward bringing more production to local communities in all 50 states, strengthening our nation’s economy, and making our country a more competitive place to produce, create, and tell great stories. We applaud President Trump’s support for this vital action, and we look forward to continuing to work with the White House and bipartisan leaders in Congress to enact a meaningful and effective national incentive into law.”

Supporters of the measure have cited a dramatic drop in domestic production since the streaming bubble burst in 2022. Around 73,000 jobs have been lost nationwide, about two-thirds of them in Los Angeles.

highlights.title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
highlights.summary: As frustration over AI influencers has been growing, Instagram is limiting the reach of undisclosed AI profiles.
body: Instagram announced Monday that it’s changing how it labels AI-generated profiles and will start limiting the reach of accounts that feature AI-generated people without saying so.

The platform says it’s renaming its existing “AI creator” label to “AI-generated profile,” which Instagram says should make the disclosure easier to understand. The new label is meant to tell users that the person featured on a profile was generated or substantially created with AI.

Under the new policy, creators who don’t properly label an AI-generated profile could see their reach reduced. Creators who use the new label, on the other hand, won’t be penalized simply for having an AI-generated person as their profile subject.

The label also isn’t meant for every use of AI. Instagram says people who use AI to edit photos, polish captions, create graphics, or make other creative tweaks don’t need to use the AI-generated profile label.

highlights.title: Pokémon World Championships 2026 Was Absolute Chaos
highlights.summary: Thousands of people descended on one of the country's busiest cities last weekend in a hunt for exclusive Pokémon merchandise, following months of retailers being unable to keep their shelves stocked with product.
body: The three-day event, which featured live Pokémon TCG tournaments and first-look opportunities for fans, was also subject to long queues and overcrowding concerns that forced the San Francisco Fire Department to step in.

One of the biggest draws of Pokémon Worlds was the Pin Rally, an opportunity for attendees to collect several exclusive pins from 12 stations throughout the Moscone Center. But with an estimated 50,000 attendees and only 8,000 exclusive pins to hand out each day, according to a report in SFGATE, crowds quickly became a concern.

On Friday, the first day of the event, at least half of the pin stations were already closed by 11 a.m. following reports of large crowds. On Saturday, people began lining up outside as early as 6 a.m. for a chance to get an exclusive pin, and crowds reportedly spilled out into the streets.
